expectations.text: Offers two or three candidate one-liners for the point, rather than one
expectations.evidence: brief.md 'Candidates considered': 'A — the sorting rule. "CLAUDE.md is for what applies every time; anything that only applies sometimes belongs in a skill."', 'B — the symptom. "Past a certain length, the rules at the bottom of CLAUDE.md stop being followed."', 'C — the trade-off (leading)... context that's always loaded but not followed, for context that might never load.'

expectations.text: Names the reader: who they are, what they believe now, what should change
expectations.evidence: Reader: Who 'A developer using Claude Code (or a similar harness) on a real, long-running repo, whose root CLAUDE.md has been growing a rule at a time'; Believes now 'Anything the agent needs to know should go in CLAUDE.md, and if a rule is being missed, the answer is to write it more firmly or add another one'; Should leave with 'Length has a cost, a test for what stays in CLAUDE.md and what moves out to a skill, and a clear sense of the risk that comes with skills (they may not load)'

Tension section: 'The file you rely on to control the agent got so long that the agent stopped following parts of it... The fix (skills) brings back a version of the same problem in a new form: now the question isn't "will it read the rule" but "will it load the skill at all".'

expectations.text: Proposes at least two arcs written as numbered beats, and recommends one with a reason
expectations.evidence: Recommended Build log as a 9-row numbered beat table; 'Alternative arc A: Single insight' beats 1-6 ('1. Default behaviour... 4. Before and after, side by side'); 'Alternative arc B: Three attempts' beats 1-8. Reason: 'what you have is concrete (one repo, ~900 → ~120 lines, six skills) and ends on an honest shortfall. That's how implementing-the-legal-framework is built'

expectations.text: Marks turning points as what the reader should see or do, not how to build a visual
expectations.evidence: 'Beat 4: the reader should see the sorting test applied', 'Beat 5: the reader should see ~900 lines shrink to ~120', 'Beat 7: the reader should feel the trade-off reverse'; no build instructions

expectations.text: Includes honesty beats (what isn't solved or what went wrong first)
expectations.evidence: Honesty beats: 'Not solved: whether skills trigger reliably. This is the planned turning point, not a disclaimer', 'What went wrong first: letting the file reach ~900 lines', 'One repo: this is one client codebase. Say so', 'What you'd do differently: author to supply'

expectations.text: Marks missing evidence as 'author to supply' (or equivalent) instead of inventing facts, numbers or anecdotes
expectations.evidence: 'author to supply' in beats 1-4, 6, 7, 9; beat 6 'don't assume it fixed the ignoring until you confirm'; position vs length 'I have not assumed it was about position rather than length... to confirm'; '"Followed when it loads" is a guess on my part. Confirm it, or drop that half'; irony hook and 'knew the principle' beat marked 'to confirm'. Cross-references verified: three-dimensions has '### 3. Selective loading beats universal loading' (l.375) and 'Every token is rent'; Legal Framework posts are titled 'Agent Harness: ...'

expectations.text: Contains no drafted body paragraphs of the post
expectations.evidence: No post prose; only candidate one-liners, titles, beat tables, emphasis plan and short hook descriptions ('Open on the numbers...', 'Open on the moment you noticed...', 'Open on the irony, if it holds...')

expectations.text: Argues the one-post-vs-series decision from the evidence in the notes
expectations.evidence: 'On one post vs a series: a series only works if each part stands alone and answers one question... You can answer part 1 now. Part 2 has no evidence yet: your notes say you're not sure. So write one post, end it on the open triggering question'; response.md 'one post, not a series, at least for now'

expectations.text: Plans an honesty beat around skills not triggering reliably
expectations.evidence: Beat 7 'What's not right yet: do skills trigger reliably? (turning point 2)' with 'author to supply. Notes only say "not sure"'; Honesty beats 'This is the planned turning point, not a disclaimer.'

expectations.text: Shows what at least two candidate phrasings of the point would each include or leave out
expectations.evidence: Each candidate has explicit scope: A '*Includes:* the criterion you used to decide what moved... *Leaves out:* the failure that pushed you to do it, and the triggering doubt'; B '*Includes:* the failure, how you noticed it... *Leaves out:* most of the skills migration'; C '*Includes:* the failure, the migration, the before/after, and the unresolved triggering question... *Leaves out:* a definitive "skills are the answer" claim'

expectations.text: Leaves the brief unlocked and runs (or explicitly defers until the wording is chosen) a check of every beat against the point's wording
expectations.evidence: 'Status: **Draft**'; 'Nothing below is locked until you pick the wording, and the beat check runs against whatever you pick'; 'Beat check: not run yet. It runs once you pick the wording. Watch for: if you pick A, beats 7–8 ... become a footnote; if you pick B, beats 4–6 shrink to one.'
